sanskrit_verse:
ṛtvik tu trividho dṛṣṭaḥ pūrvajuṣṭaḥ svayaṃkṛtaḥ ।
 yadṛcchayā ca yaḥ kuryād ārtvijyaṃ prītipūrvakam ॥
transliteration: ṛtvik tu trividho dṛṣṭaḥ pūrvajuṣṭaḥ svayaṃkṛtaḥ | yadṛcchayā ca yaḥ kuryād ārtvijyaṃ prītipūrvakam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The officiant is threefold: one who performs by prior instruction, one who acts on his own initiative, and one who undertakes the duty spontaneously out of joy.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from conscious capacity to act in alignment with Dharma
Causation arises from volitional engagement, not external compulsion
Capacity-based responsibility determines the scope of lawful action
Restoration occurs through spontaneous right action rooted in inner integrity
Consciousness alignment manifests as joyful participation in universal order
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent performs ritual/service due to prior instruction THEN responsibility binding only to extent of received capacity
IF agent initiates action autonomously THEN full operational authority granted within svadharma bounds
IF agent engages spontaneously with joy THEN maximum restoration potential activated
ALL agents must be evaluated based on consciousness-state during execution, not outcome alone
NO punitive consequence shall arise; restoration protocols apply universally
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, the tripartite nature of agency must determine threshold of legal responsibility. One acting under directive bears limited liability compared to autonomous actor. Highest recognition belongs to spontaneous joyful service which reflects pure consciousness alignment. Courts must assess not just act but ontological state at time of performance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that causal chain originates in willful engagement. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential unfolding from intention to completion. Responsibility is proportional to awareness and freedom of choice. Since punishment has no place in reality, all misalignments are resolved through reintegration into source-consciousness where rectification occurs naturally.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Ensure interrupted or incomplete actions are finalized according to original intent
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Encourage willing resumption of duty until harmonious conclusion
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Realign individual consciousness with innate ability to serve Dharma
Integrity Reintegration Sequence: Facilitate return to spontaneous joyful participation in cosmic order
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established. The officiant's role is defined not by coercion nor reward, but by alignment with eternal consciousness. Justice serves restoration alone. Reality knows no punishment. Consciousness itself is the ultimate judge.
